text: Star args and double-star kwargs let a function accept any number of arguments.
Star args collects every positional argument into a tuple called args.
So total just sums that tuple, however many numbers you pass in.
Even calling it with no arguments works, because sum of an empty tuple is zero.
Double-star kwargs does the same for keyword arguments, collecting them into a dictionary.
We join the key value pairs into one readable string.
The names args and kwargs are only convention — the stars do the actual work.
Four numbers in, and total adds them all to ten.
Profile takes name and age as keywords and formats them back out.
The star works in the other direction too, when you're calling rather than defining.
Star nums unpacks the list into three separate arguments, giving sixty.
One star unpacks a sequence, and two stars unpack a dictionary into keywords.
